title: Filesystem mutation completion
objective: Close the everyday filesystem gaps recorded by the SG-000059 inventory with individually reviewed, bounded operations inside the workspace ceiling: create directory, move or rename, delete, exact search-and-replace edit bound to the current file digest, ranged text read, and bounded file-name search, each with final Windows path identity, protected-path denial, destructive approval where an operation removes or overwrites, and postcondition verification, exposed as static MCP tools with no unrestricted filesystem primitive.

include: fs_mkdir: create one directory (optionally its missing parents) inside a trusted workspace with SOFT approval and postcondition verification
fs_move: move or rename one file or directory within the same workspace, never overwriting, with SOFT approval bound to source identity and postcondition verification
fs_delete: delete one file or one empty directory bound to its current digest or identity with STRONG-class destructive approval and postcondition verification; no recursive delete
fs_edit: exact search-and-replace on one text file bound to its current SHA-256 with a bounded number of replacements and SOFT approval
fs_read_range: bounded line-range read of one text file
fs_find: bounded file-name glob search inside a workspace without following links
final path identity, workspace ceiling, protected-path and reparse-point denial for every operation, typed failures, and regression of every existing filesystem guarantee
updates to the authoritative catalog, scope matrix, client packages, and parity inventory for the new tools
exclude: recursive delete, wildcard mutation, overwrite on move, permission or attribute changes, link creation, or any path outside a trusted workspace
browser, desktop, clipboard, or network exposure (SG-000062 through SG-000064)

authority_delta.filesystem: Bounded mkdir, move or rename without overwrite, single-file or empty-directory delete with destructive approval, digest-bound exact edit, ranged read, and name search inside trusted workspaces.
authority_delta.approval: Mutations require fresh per-action approval; delete requires the destructive approval class.

invariants: no filesystem operation leaves a trusted workspace or touches protected state
links, junctions, and reparse points are never followed or created
every mutation is approved, digest- or identity-bound, and postcondition-verified
no recursive or wildcard mutation exists

acceptance.claim: The six operations work inside a trusted workspace with approval, digest or identity binding, and postcondition verification.
Escapes, protected paths, reparse points, overwrite, recursive delete, stale digests, denied approvals, and oversized inputs fail closed without mutation.
Exact-head CI including release qualification and supply-chain audit, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.sg_000062: Structured browser MCP exposure may proceed only after SG-000061 closes.

done_when: Bounded filesystem mutation is canonical with workspace ceilings, approvals, identity binding, and postcondition verification and no unrestricted filesystem primitive.
